summary: The prompt over-splits at conditional/contrastive connectives that tightly bind a clause to its result, causing restructuring, tense mismatch, register shift, or name mistranslation, while simultaneously under-splitting long multi-clause sentences that have obvious safe boundaries (て-chains, し-coordination, temporal/resultative clauses). Segmentation decisions need to be based on clause independence rather than punctuation position alone.
